what_it_does: Copies the dx-toolkit Python source into a fresh temporary directory and runs the macOS test suite for one Python environment inside it.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The copy is a local 19 MB tree that is small next to the venv build and pip install that follow. run_tests.sh installs from that tree with pip, which can write build output into it, so one shared copy would race when workers is above 1.

what_it_does: Copies the source tree into a temporary directory, creates a venv there, and runs pytest for one Windows Python environment.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The copy is a local 19 MB tree, small next to the venv creation and pip install that follow. pip installs from that tree and can write build output into it, so each environment and each retry needs its own copy to avoid carrying state between runs.

what_it_does: Builds the Docker test image for one Python environment, pulling the base image first, and writes the build log to disk.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Pulling is the default and the documented behaviour, and --no-docker-pull exists to turn it off, so the repair would change which base image gets tested. Each pull is one registry manifest check against a full image build, so the saving is small.

what_it_does: Installs each requested pyenv or brew Python version in turn, runs the per-environment test workers, and writes the execution summary.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Dropping the force flag changes what brew does to a broken or unlinked formula, and a skip changes the output written to the install log at line 106 on every run. The energy saved is real, but the repair changes machine state and logged output, so it is rejected.

what_it_does: Writes a local test file, either 100 MB of random bytes or the given text, uploads it with dx upload, and polls dx describe until the file is closed.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The wait is needed because dx upload without --wait returns while the file is still closing, so the loop normally makes a few polls. Passing --wait would move the wait into one process with backoff, but the failure path would change: today it raises an AssertionError after about 200 seconds, while the repair would wait up to a day inside dx and print different error text.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Random content is generated in one test call at line 168, and the kernel took about half a second to produce 100 MB here, which is small beside the 100 MB upload that follows. Writing zeros would change the uploaded bytes for a saving too small to justify that change.

what_it_does: Logs a pass or fail line for each environment, optionally writes the results to a JSON report, and returns the overall exit code.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The list is built once per summary over at most 21 entries, so replacing it with a generator saves nothing measurable.

what_it_does: Returns a urllib3 connection pool that is cached for default settings, and builds a fresh uncached pool on every call when verify, cert_file, key_file, ssl_context or DX_CA_CERT is set.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each uncached call builds a new pool, so every request opens a new TCP connection and TLS handshake. A single-slot cache keyed on verify, cert_file, key_file, ssl_context, DX_CA_CERT, DX_USE_OS_CA_BUNDLE and the proxy variable reuses the pool, the proxy message still prints on every call, and the error path clear call at line 727 then acts on the pool that was used, which is what that call intends.

what_it_does: Walks the resources directory, computes a checksum from file metadata, reuses a matching bundle if one exists, and otherwise tars, gzips and uploads the tree.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The checksum uses only stat data, yet the code reads and writes every resource file into an uncompressed tar before it looks for a matching bundle. The repair runs a metadata-only first walk that opens each regular file, never a FIFO, so an unreadable file still raises the same error before any lookup, and it builds the archive only when no bundle matches, so the reuse path skips every content read and tar write.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The finished uncompressed tar is re-read in 8 KB chunks and gzipped into a second temp file, which costs one full write and one full read of the archive on the upload path. Writing the gzip stream directly with tarfile in w:gz mode gives the same tar entries at compression level 9, so only the gzip header timestamp and temp file name differ, as they already do between runs.

what_it_does: Creates or updates an app version from its spec, syncs its categories, developers and authorized users, and publishes it or tags it as the default.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The authorized-user list at line 900 is needed when the spec has authorizedUsers or when brief is False. With brief True and no authorizedUsers its result is unused, but a failure of that call raises today, so skipping it would silence an error on an input the current code accepts, and the saving is one read-only request per brief build.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The next form returns the same boolean, but list() requests a second page only when the search reports more results, so the repair also removes a request whose failure raises today. That is the same kind of change as line 900, and the saving is one request for apps with two or more published versions.

what_it_does: Uploads the asset config, makefile and tarball, starts the asset builder job, waits for it to finish, and prints the resulting asset ID.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The job is polled with a describe once per second for the whole build. An interval of 10 seconds gives the same return value and the same failure path, cuts state requests about tenfold, and adds at most ten seconds at the end of the build.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The call is the credential check that runs before any upload, so removing it changes which call fails first and the text printed for a bad token, which would then come from dx_upload. The saving is one request per asset build.

what_it_does: Returns the billTo for a build, defaulting to the caller's own billTo and checking that a user or org value is allowed.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: For an org billTo the user id is not used, so the whoami call could move, but the org_describe call sits inside a bare except. With an invalid token today the DXAPIError from whoami propagates, while the repair would turn the same auth failure into the builder exception, so the exception type changes.

what_it_does: Checks the executables of each workflow stage, recursing into inner workflows, and narrows the set of regions in which the workflow can be enabled.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each applet stage describes its project and that project's region again, and each app stage describes the same app again, so every repeated stage costs one request. A memo keyed on executable and project id, passed through the recursion with a None default, returns the same values, and the first failing describe still raises as before.

what_it_does: Lists every notebook app version and returns each version string by describing each app separately.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop makes one app describe per version just to read the version string. A find_apps call with describe set returns that field inside the search that already runs, and utils/completer.py already reads result['describe'] from find_apps, so the list is the same and the per-app requests go away, provided the search describe includes version on the platform.

what_it_does: Polls the job every 5 seconds until the notebook server tag appears or the job fails, then exits with advice if it failed.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each poll fetches the full job description, including inputs and outputs that the loop never reads. Asking only for state and tags keeps the loop, the request count and the failure message unchanged, so each poll sends and parses a smaller payload, which is a small saving, and the platform must accept those field names.

what_it_does: Returns the message unchanged if its JSON form fits in 8015 characters, otherwise cuts it to a JSON-safe prefix with a truncation marker.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The trim runs json.dumps once per byte removed, up to about 4000 times for non-ASCII or escape-heavy text, but the 8000 byte slice at line 77 caps the cost, so the cost is bounded and not quadratic in message size. A binary search over the prefix length returned identical output on 400 random inputs that I checked, and it cut a 12000 character CJK message from 0.11 s to 0.4 ms.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The whole message is encoded and serialised once just to measure it, which is linear in the message and costs a few microseconds for typical records. That is too small to justify an edit to a logging path.

what_it_does: Looks up each cacheable image reference in the project image cache, sets its file ID on a hit, and prints one progress line per reference.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Duplicate references repeat an identical find_data_objects search, one request per process that uses the image. A memo keyed on cache folder, cache file name and digest, storing only successful results, lets each reference still set its file ID and print its line, and failed lookups stay unmemoized so their warnings repeat as before; the existing test at test_nextflow_collect_images.py line 336 asserts two calls and would need to assert one.

what_it_does: Runs docker manifest inspect with up to two retries after 60 and 300 seconds, and returns the parsed JSON or None.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The sleeps are idle time, which costs little energy, and each retry adds one more docker manifest inspect run, which is a registry request. The retries exist for transient registry and network errors, and a no-retry repair would turn those into a None digest for a valid image, so the behaviour changes.

what_it_does: Starts the Nextflow importer job, waits for it to finish by polling once per second, and returns the applet ID.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The importer job is polled with a describe once per second until it finishes. An interval of 10 seconds gives the same applet ID and the same failure path, cuts state requests about tenfold, and adds at most ten seconds at the end of the import.

what_it_does: Tars the app directory, uploads the archive, starts the remote builder job, optionally watches it, waits for it to finish, and returns the applet ID.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: With watch off, the remote build job is polled once per second, and an app build runs for minutes. An interval of 10 seconds keeps the return value and the failure path and cuts state requests about tenfold, at the cost of up to ten seconds of latency.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The loop spins only between the end of tar's stdout and tar being reaped, since read blocks while data flows, so the spin lasts about as long as tar takes to exit. That window is normally very short, and a sleep would add latency for little energy gain.

what_it_does: Returns the bundledDepends entry for one image, caching it on the platform when no file ID is known and otherwise describing the existing file to get its name.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The describe at line 93 is needed because the name is not kept on the _ImageRef record, so removing the call means carrying the name through the collect_docker_images output. That changes the documented return keys of that function, and the saving is one describe per cache hit.

what_it_does: Pulls a Docker image with sudo docker, saves it as a gzip tarball, uploads the tarball to the project cache, and returns the uploaded file ID.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The pull is the only source of image layers when the image is absent locally, and for a mutable tag it refreshes the local copy so the saved tarball matches the registry. Skipping it when a local copy exists would upload a stale tag, which changes the file written, and for digest-pinned refs the skipped work is one manifest request beside a save, gzip and upload that still run.

what_it_does: Syntax-checks the entry point, the bootstrap scripts and every file under resources, and warns about resource files that fail.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Passing the enforce flag through would stop the DXSyntaxError raise, which removes the files-with-problems warning under the no-check-syntax option, and skipping the call would also remove the per-file error lines printed by the check. Both are printed output, and the work saved is a py_compile per resource .py file and a bash -n per .sh file, which is small local CPU.

what_it_does: Checks an app or applet source tree, chooses build projects by region, uploads resources and the executable, and creates or returns the app or applet.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: On the applet branch with a destination, the region of the same working project is described at line 793 and again at line 845 inside a try block. When the second project equals the one already described, the second call can reuse the region from the first, which yields the same region and projects_by_region, and the first call already raises before the second could run. The removed call is one identical API request per applet build with a destination.

what_it_does: Warns when dxapp.json suggestions name projects, folders or objects that are missing or not public, and raises when a suggested object is absent.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each suggestion with a project sends its own project describe, so a project named by several inputs is described repeatedly. A per-call memo keyed by project and the permissions flag, holding either the response or the DXAPIError, keeps every warning and every exception path the same, and the saving is a few API round trips per build.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The describe call is the existence test that raises on a 404, so only the unused assignment could be removed, which saves nothing, and removing the call would drop the error.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: Each suggestion with a path issues its own folder listing, so repeated project and path pairs repeat the request. Memoizing the outcome per pair, including a ResolutionError that is re-raised unchanged, keeps the warning and abort behaviour identical.

what_it_does: Routes a build to the Nextflow path, the build-from-applet path, a local build, or a remote build, and returns or prints the executable ID.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The list in the any call holds two items and is_importer_job reads one small local JSON file, each once per invocation, so the energy at stake is microseconds.

what_it_does: Creates a temporary applet directory, copies the template tree into it, and writes the generated dxapp.json, source script and readme.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The copied dxapp.json and src/nextflow.sh are overwritten later, but copy2 keeps the template mode on src/nextflow.sh, while a file created fresh by the write call gets a umask-dependent mode, so the file written changes. The saving is a 42 KB local copy.

what_it_does: Checks that the version asset files and the project ID files parse, hold well-formed IDs, and list the same regions in prod and staging.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The premise fails, because versions.json names distinct files for 24.10 and 25.10, so no asset file is processed twice, and each file is about 600 bytes.

what_it_does: Returns the alphabetically first regular file in a directory whose name matches a readme pattern, or None.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The re module caches compiled patterns, so compile is a cache lookup, and the stat calls run once per build over the top-level entries, which costs microseconds.

what_it_does: Runs the interactive app wizard, printing instance-type tables and prompting for app settings, and fills in the app spec.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: It runs once per interactive session on a table of preferred types, so the list it builds costs microseconds next to the user typing.

what_it_does: Lists the folders and objects at a path or the matched entities, printing names, IDs, or long-form descriptions.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The folder-path Counter at line 815 is already gated on brief and verbose, and the unconditional Counter at line 827 is one pass of dictionary increments over the matched results, microseconds per entry, which is small next to the describe payload that produced those results.

what_it_does: Removes the named objects and folders, after a recursive pre-check that warns about removing a whole project, and reports paths that fail to resolve.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Reusing the pre-check resolution would drop the second interactive prompt for an ambiguous name, because resolve_existing_path with allow_mult prompts in an interactive session and the main loop calls it again. The output and user interaction would change, and the saving is only a few API round trips.

what_it_does: Sets the current project and working folder after resolving the path and checking that the folder can be listed.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: When the describe is moved into the branch that uses it, a failing describe in the skipped case would no longer exit with the describe error at line 737, so the error path and its message change, which breaks the same-output rule.

what_it_does: Describes a data object, execution or project named by a path or ID and prints the result in the chosen format.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The probe decides whether the project hint is sent, since ResourceNotFound omits the hint, other errors raise, and success adds it. Removing the probe changes behaviour for an inaccessible workspace, and a fallback path would need to match each exception path exactly, which is not shown.

what_it_does: Downloads the non-directory files of a database object, listing them first and writing each under the output path.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The debug calls format whole objects, including the full database file listing, before logging.debug discards them at the INFO level set by basicConfig. Switching these calls to lazy %s logging gives the same text when debug is on and skips the formatting otherwise, and the saving is CPU that scales with listing size, which is unmeasured because real listings are not in the repository.

what_it_does: Finds executions matching the query and prints each root with its retries and stage tree, optionally as JSON.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The roots mapping is an OrderedDict with one entry per root in a result page, so building a key list to test emptiness copies a few entries, which costs microseconds.

what_it_does: Builds the run request for an executable from the arguments, merges cloned and overriding system requirements, prints warnings, and submits the run.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The deep copy protects args.cloned_job_desc, because the system requirements objects share nested dicts with it and the merge calls at lines 3254, 3277 and 3278 update dicts in place. Removing the copy would alter the arguments, and the copy costs milliseconds.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Each workflow stage sends its own describe of its executable, so stages that share an executable ID repeat the same request. A memo keyed by that ID gives the same set of special access strings, because adding the same spec to a set is idempotent, and a failing describe still raises at its first occurrence. It runs only with an explicit priority of low or normal and without brief.

what_it_does: Produces tab-completion candidates for dx command words, paths, and app names for run, install and uninstall.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The class DXCLICompleter is never instantiated anywhere in the repository, since a grep finds only its definition, so no TAB press reaches this code and the energy claim has no caller to measure.

what_it_does: Opens an SSH session to a job by waiting for it to run, waiting for its host and host key, checking connectivity, and then launching ssh.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Both wait loops describe the job every second with no backoff. Describing on a doubling interval capped at 8 seconds, with the one-second sleep and the dot per iteration kept, cuts API requests to about one eighth after the first half minute. The trade-off is that a start or host key may be noticed up to 8 seconds late, and the printed output keeps the same form.

what_it_does: Tags files or a folder for archival or unarchival in one project, resolving the paths, optionally confirming, and sending the request.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Batching names by folder would replace k name-filtered searches with one folder search that returns every object in the folder, which can move more data, and the per-name pick prompts would have to be rebuilt on top of the batched result. The direction of the energy change is not established.

what_it_does: Looks up gene bin entries for a list of gene names in a platform manifest fetched with a dx cat subprocess, and returns the positions with strand removed.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Every call repeats a project describe, a platform file describe, a new dx cat process that downloads the manifest, and a JSON parse. A module-level cache keyed by project, reference, base path and manifest names, holding the parsed manifest and a per-call deep copy of each entry used, keeps the returned entries and the duplicate-gene KeyError identical. It goes stale only if the manifest is republished during one process, and the size of the saved download is unknown because the repository holds only 868-byte stubs.

what_it_does: Validates a user filter for the allele, annotation or genotype retrieval types by calling validate_filter, after first opening and parsing a packaged schema file whose result is discarded.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The schema read is one small local JSON file per CLI invocation, since dataset_utilities.py line 631 calls this once per filter, so the saved work is microseconds. The open at line 296 is also the only check that the packaged schema file exists, so removing it changes the exception raised when that asset is missing.

what_it_does: Adds an entity field filter to a cohort pheno filter by intersecting or subtracting the requested IDs with the values already stored in the filter, converting those stored values with a caller-supplied reduce function.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The quadratic copying happens inside the caller lambda passed as lambda_for_list_conv, which is defined in validate_cohort_ids at dataset_utilities.py lines 1750 to 1754, so no edit inside this function removes it. Calling the lambda once per element would match the reduce result only if every caller lambda has the form a plus a one-element list, and the signature does not guarantee that.

what_it_does: Writes a new app skeleton from template files and, for each matching code template, renders the language-specific code strings from the app spec.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Both get_strings implementations, in bash.py and python.py, ignore the dummy_output_hash argument, and the dict is built once per code template in an interactive wizard run, which is microseconds of work. Removing it would also change the get_strings signature for both languages, and the energy gain is below anything measurable.

what_it_does: Checks that the infer-ref and infer-nocall flags agree with the exclusion parameters recorded at ingestion, exiting through err_exit on a mismatch.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The f-string costs well under a microsecond and runs once per CLI invocation through inference_validation, so the saving is negligible. Building it only on the error paths would preserve behaviour, but the energy gain is too small to justify the edit.

what_it_does: Builds the top-level query payload for one filter type, loading the matching return_columns JSON file to set the fields and the ordering.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each read is a 322 to 530 byte file, and the function runs at most four times per genotype run from dataset_utilities.py lines 1007 to 1042, with each run already making several HTTP queries that cost far more energy. Caching the parsed list would share one fields list across payloads, and line 1069 of dataset_utilities.py appends to the genotype_only_payload fields, so a shared list would leak that column into other payloads.

what_it_does: Rewrites a genotype-only SQL statement so its locus join and SELECT list line up with the genotype and allele union, rereading the genotype return column list on each call.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The file is 401 bytes and the function runs at most three times per germline run from the loop at dataset_utilities.py lines 1067 to 1072, so the reread costs microseconds next to the HTTP query on either side of it. A module-level load would preserve behaviour, but the saving is below anything measurable.

what_it_does: Streams one database file to disk in ranged chunks through a thread pool, with a describe call before the write and a retry on DXFileError.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: An MD5 digest is computed over every downloaded byte and never read, because its only consumer, verify_part, is called only from the two commented-out lines 256 and 266, so removing the hasher, the verify calls and the got_bytes count stops one MD5 pass over the data with no change to return values, files, output or exceptions. The TODO at line 255 suggests the check may be removed for good, and re-enabling it later would bring this cost back.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The describe result is unused, but it is the only check that runs before ensure_local_dir at line 198 and the open at lines 211 to 213 create anything on disk, so skipping it on the first attempt changes what is left behind for a missing database. Retries happen only after a DXFileError, so the repeat saves one call per failed part, which is rare.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: Each do_debug call formats one short string, and the call in get_chunk runs once per chunk, which is about 6,400 formats for a 100 GB file at the 16 MiB chunk size used outside a job, each costing about a microsecond. That is negligible beside the thousands of multi-megabyte HTTP reads the same download makes.

what_it_does: Returns a download URL and its headers for a database file, caching the URL on the handler and calling the API for it on first use or after expiry.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The existence check runs before the cache test, so a caller that passes a DXDatabase handler with a project and project None pays one describe per chunk, although its result is needed only when the URL is refreshed. Moving the check under the refresh branch would change what the _DX_DUMP_BILLED_PROJECT hook writes on cached calls at lines 186 to 189, and it would stop raising a describe error that the current code raises mid-download.

what_it_does: Polls the analysis state with a describe call every interval seconds until the analysis is done, and raises on failure, termination or timeout.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each poll is a real API request, and the default 2 second interval over a 7 day timeout allows about 302,400 requests, so the waste holds. Backoff would break the docstring contract that interval is the number of seconds between queries, which a caller sets on purpose, so the change needs a decision from the API owner rather than an energy-only edit.

what_it_does: Downloads, decompresses and parses the dataset descriptor, then groups its assays by generalized model type into a new dictionary on every access.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each access downloads and parses the full descriptor, and one extract_assay_expression run reads this property four to six times, so caching the built dict on the instance leaves one download per object. The repair uses self.__dict__ because DXObject.__getattr__ would issue a describe request for a missing attribute, and it returns the cached object, which no caller in the repo mutates, with the same staleness limit as the existing detail_describe cache.

what_it_does: Returns the assay names for one generalized model type by reading the assays_info_dict property.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The function reads the uncached property twice, so each call downloads and parses the descriptor twice, and binding the property to one local variable makes it once with the same return value and the same first-access exception. The repair stands on its own, and it becomes redundant once the cache on assays_info_dict is applied.

what_it_does: Returns the assay record whose uuid matches the argument by scanning the assays_info_dict property.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The one access on line 114 costs one descriptor download per call, and no edit to this function removes it, because only the cache in assays_info_dict removes that download, and that cache is accepted under its own unit.

what_it_does: Returns the index of the assay with a given name by scanning the assays_info_dict property.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The one access on line 130 costs one descriptor download per call, and the same reasoning applies, since the cache accepted under assays_info_dict removes it and no edit to this function does.

what_it_does: Checks that each genomic range in a list ends after it starts and, optionally, that the total span fits a window width, reporting violations through the error handler.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The repeated int conversions run on a short user-supplied list of location ranges, each costing well under a microsecond, and the function runs once per extract_assay_expression call at dataset_utilities.py line 1601. The saving is below anything measurable.

what_it_does: Creates the input directory tree, downloads every non-excluded file input into it, and returns helper variables that give the local path, name and prefix of each downloaded file.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The describe in get_job_input_filenames is the only source of each local file name, since job_input.json holds only link IDs, so it cannot be removed. The other describe for the same file, inside the download, is decision b, and it is the one that could be merged.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: download_dxfile needs the parts field in its describe_output, and the name describe in file_load_utils.get_job_input_filenames does not fetch it, so merging the two calls requires changing that shared helper, which analyze_bash_vars and other callers use. The name describe is made through a link handler while the download describe runs without a project, so the two can see different project contexts and a merge could change which context is described.

what_it_does: Builds the path, name and prefix lists for each input variable by rerunning analyze_bash_vars on the job input file.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: analyze_bash_vars calls get_job_input_filenames, which builds a handler and makes a describe request for each file again, and the caller already holds the same trg_fname values in its inputs argument, so building the lists from that argument removes one describe per file input and one parse of job_input.json. The prefix rule is copied from analyze_bash_vars and still uses get_input_spec_patterns, so the lists match element for element, and the shared file_load_utils module stays unchanged.

what_it_does: Builds the path, name and prefix lists for each mounted input variable by rerunning analyze_bash_vars on the job input file after the dxfuse mount is up.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: This is the download variant, because analyze_bash_vars repeats one describe per mounted file and one parse of job_input.json that mount_all_inputs already did for the same entries, so building the lists from the inputs argument removes those calls and returns the same dict. The prefix rule is copied as in the download variant, which leaves file_load_utils unchanged.

what_it_does: Creates the in directory, writes a dxfuse manifest for the file inputs, mounts it, lists the mount tree to stdout, and returns helper variables.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The find output goes to stdout, which lands in the job log, so removing it changes the printed output a job produces. A Python directory walk would make the same directory reads and would save no energy.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Two id subprocesses cost a few milliseconds of process startup once per job, which is too small to measure, so the edit saves nothing that matters even though os.geteuid and os.getegid return the values that id -u and id -g print.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: One mkdir fork per job is negligible energy, and replacing it with os.mkdir would change the exception from CalledProcessError to FileExistsError when the mount directory already exists.

what_it_does: Accepts str, bytearray, bytes or mmap data, converts it to bytes, and passes it to _write2 for buffered upload.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The bytes copy is needed because _write2 at line 492 and upload_part at line 645 both assert that data is bytes, so passing the mmap through fails at those asserts. Fixing that means changing upload_part, which lies outside this unit, and as a result the zero-copy branch in _write2 never receives an mmap object.

what_it_does: Buffers written bytes into fixed-size upload parts, sends each full part to upload_part, and recurses through write for the tail of a write that spans more than the free buffer space.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each recursion copies the remaining tail at line 532, so one large write copies roughly n squared over 2B bytes, but the recursive call also drops the multithread argument because write is called with its default True, so a loop would have to reproduce that quirk. The recursion also raises RecursionError for writes spanning roughly 500 buffers, and a loop would remove that exception on those inputs, which changes the exception raised for them.

what_it_does: Yields the lines of a remote file opened in text mode by reading fixed-size chunks through read and splitting the accumulated buffer on newlines.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: A partial line is re-split on every chunk, so a line longer than the read chunk (16 MiB by default) costs quadratic scanning. A repair that keeps a list of pending pieces and splits only when a chunk holds a newline, found with rfind, scans each byte once and yields the same lines and the same trailing piece, and the saving touches only lines longer than the read chunk.

what_it_does: Downloads the chunks of a remote file in parallel into a local file, checks each part against its md5 or checksum, and returns False so download_dxfile can retry after a recoverable part error.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: On a retry the rb+ branch re-reads and re-hashes every part already on disk, but skipping that check would change the result when the local file is altered between attempts, because the check truncates the file at the first part that no longer matches. Skipping only parts verified in the same call sequence needs new state threaded through a private helper that test_dxfile_download.py calls directly, so the repair would not preserve behaviour on every input.

what_it_does: Uploads a local file or file-like object into a new platform file in buffered parts and retries the whole upload up to twice when the parts do not finish closing.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each retry creates a new file object and re-uploads the whole local file, but wait_until_parts_uploaded raises DXError only after its 255 second timeout and reports no failed part, so the retry cannot be narrowed to the missing parts. Reusing the first handler would change the returned file ID and leave the abandoned file on the platform.

what_it_does: Checks the md5 of a local file by running the md5sum executable found on PATH and exits through err_exit on a mismatch or a failed run.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The subprocess costs one fork and exec per symlink download, which is small next to reading and hashing the file, and both paths read the file once. Switching to md5_hasher would also remove the missing md5sum exit and change the mismatch message, which prints a bytes repr of the digest today, so the observable output would change.

what_it_does: Returns the workflow description for one region of a global workflow by describing its regional underlying workflow, with a per-region cache that never hits.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The write at line 194 replaces the whole dict, so the check at line 181 always misses, but every caller in the repo, exec_io.py line 433, dx.py line 3461 through append_underlying_workflow_desc, and executable_unbuilder.py line 372, runs this once per object, so the repair would avoid no describe call. A cache hit would also return a stale description when describe_output differs, because the cache check runs before describe_output is read.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: After get_underlying_workflow runs on the same handle, line 226 leaves a DXWorkflow object in _workflow_desc_by_region, and the membership test at line 181 then raises TypeError, which a stand-in class confirms because DXWorkflow defines no container dunder. That is a crash rather than wasted work, and removing line 226 would change the exception on that input, so it belongs in a correctness fix.

what_it_does: Returns a DXWorkflow handle for the underlying workflow of one region, describing the global workflow first when no description is passed in.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The cache _workflows_by_region is read at line 215 but never written, so each stage-qualified input in exec_io.py line 777 builds a new handle whose first stages access costs one workflow describe, and caching dxid-based handles by region removes those repeats since globalworkflow IDs are immutable (name and alias handles stay uncached because an alias can move between calls). Cache hits skip the global describe and the region check, so a later loss of access goes unreported by this lookup while the run call still checks it, and line 226 stays as it is.

what_it_does: Builds the run input for a global workflow by looking up the region of the target project and delegating to the underlying workflow for that region.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: A project region does not change, so the project_describe at line 262 repeats on every run through the same handle, and caching the region per non-None project in a dict created in __init__ removes that request. The saving is one small API call per repeated run and none for the one-shot CLI, and a cache hit skips the access check for that project, which the run call still makes.

what_it_does: Polls one job state describe per interval until the job is done, has failed, or the timeout passes.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop sends a describe every fixed interval, 2 seconds by default, for up to seven days, so a one-hour job makes about 1800 requests. Sleeping min(interval times 2 to the i, max of interval and 128), the same cap that DXDataObject._wait_on_close in bindings/__init__.py uses, cuts an hour to about 35 requests, and keeping interval as the floor and adding the real sleep to elapsed leaves the timeout, the return value, and the exceptions unchanged, at the cost of up to 128 seconds of extra latency after completion.

what_it_does: Removes a folder through repeated partial removal requests until the server reports the removal completed.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: With partial set to true each request removes a batch of objects on the server, so the requests are not redundant, and a sleep would lengthen wall-clock time without lowering the request count. The repo gives no sign of a response that reports completed false without progress, and that is the only case where the back-to-back loop would waste energy.

what_it_does: Wraps a system find call in a generator that pages through results until the consumer limit or the final page is reached.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: When the limit is reached exactly at the end of a page that has a next token, the generator fetches the following page after the consumer takes the last allowed item, because the limit check runs only at the next yield. Testing num_results == limit right after each yield returns before that request and yields the same items, so a consumer such as list sees no difference.

what_it_does: Adds an executable as a stage through workflow_add_stage, then refreshes the cached workflow description in a finally block.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The describe refreshes _desc, which __getattr__ serves for editVersion, stages, and every other key, so a describe restricted to editVersion and stages would drop the other keys and make later reads raise AttributeError. Deferring the refresh with _desc set to an empty dict would save one describe per chain of mutations only, and it would move any describe error from this call to a later read.

what_it_does: Removes a stage through workflow_remove_stage, then refreshes the cached workflow description in a finally block.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The describe at line 274 is the only refresh of _desc after the mutation, and later editVersion and stages reads depend on it, so a restricted describe would drop keys. Deferring it would save one describe per chain of mutations only, for the same reasons given for add_stage.

what_it_does: Moves a stage to a new index through workflow_move_stage, then refreshes the cached workflow description in a finally block.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The describe at line 295 is the only refresh of _desc after the mutation, and later editVersion and stages reads depend on it, so a restricted describe would drop keys. Deferring it would save one describe per chain of mutations only, for the same reasons given for add_stage.

what_it_does: Applies metadata changes such as title, summary, and stages to a workflow through workflow_update, then refreshes the cached description when any change was requested.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The describe at line 365 is the only refresh of _desc after the mutation, and later editVersion and stages reads depend on it, so a restricted describe would drop keys. Deferring it would save one describe per chain of mutations only, for the same reasons given for add_stage.

what_it_does: Changes a stage executable and or its metadata through up to two workflow update calls, refreshing the cached description after each one.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The describe at line 415 supplies the editVersion that the second call at line 435 uses, so only the describe at line 437 could go, and removing it would leave a stale editVersion in _desc for the next mutation. Deferring it would save one describe only for calls that change both the executable and the metadata.

what_it_does: Resolves a stage index, stage ID, or stage name to a stage ID by reading the cached stages list.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The regex compile is served from the re module cache and a stage list holds tens of entries, so the per-call cost is microseconds. The name branch needs the full list to detect duplicate names and raise, so an early stop would change the error on that input.

what_it_does: Resolves a dataset or cohort record, selects a molecular expression assay, validates the filters, and writes expression data fetched from vizserver to the output file.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Dataset.assays_info_dict and descriptor_file_dict each download and parse the descriptor on every access, which happens six times without --assay-name and four times with it. Memoizing the parsed descriptor inside descriptor_file_dict in src/python/dxpy/bindings/apollo/dataset.py cuts those fetches to one, since every reader builds new structures from it and nothing mutates it, so the outputs stay the same.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: DATASET_DESCRIPTOR is assigned here and never read in this function or anywhere else in the repo, so the line is one more full descriptor fetch for nothing. Removing it changes behaviour only if this one download fails while the earlier fetches of the same file succeeded.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: resolve_existing_path describes the record with default fields at line 1401, and resolve_cohort_to_dataset describes it again at line 1433 to get properties and details that the first call lacks. Asking for those fields in the first describe, which accepts a describe dict and passes it to the find call at search.py line 259, and giving resolve_cohort_to_dataset an optional precomputed description that its one-argument test callers can omit, removes one describe request per path invocation.

what_it_does: Converts the supplied cohort IDs to the key type of the primary entity, queries vizserver for the matching rows, and returns the converted list along with the converter lambda.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The reduce with a+[int(b)] or its float and str variants copies the accumulated list at every step, so N IDs cost about N squared over two element copies, and 50,000 string IDs took 11.7 seconds in a timing run here against 0.005 seconds for a comprehension. A list comprehension over the same converter returns the same list and raises the same ValueError on bad input, and the returned lambda is kept because generate_pheno_filter in src/python/dxpy/dx_extract_utils/cohort_filter_payload.py uses it at lines 37 and 39, where the same quadratic reduce runs and needs its own repair.

what_it_does: Builds a coding dataframe with one row per code, carrying meaning, concept, and display order, and walks a node tree when the coding is hierarchical.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The membership test and the index call each scan the display list for every code, so the cost grows as codes times display length, and 8,000 codes took 1.05 seconds in a timing run here. A dict of first positions built once, with setdefault so that the first index wins as index does, gives the same display_order values, and the repair runs only when display is a list, so a malformed display still takes the original path and raises the same error.

what_it_does: Builds one entity dataframe per entity, then writes relationship and reference fields into the source entity frame for each join edge.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The result of assign is bound to a local that is never read, since the next pass of the loop rebinds source_eblock from eblocks, so each edge copies a whole entity frame for nothing. Dropping those lines leaves the in-place writes through values at lines 2061 to 2066 unchanged, and assign never modifies its input, so eblocks ends in the same state.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The full-column comparison runs once per edge and feeds both the uniqueness check at line 2058 and the write at line 2063, so it cannot be removed. A vector comparison over one entity field rows costs microseconds per edge, so the energy involved is negligible.

what_it_does: Pages through the viz-meta codings endpoint, merges coding fragments that the server split across pages, rebuilds split hierarchies, and returns all codings keyed by name.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The page dict is local to one pass of the loop and nothing else holds it, so the deepcopy at line 278 duplicates every coding tree for no reader. Storing the page object directly returns the same content with the same requests, and the only divergence is for a transport that hands back an object the caller still holds, which JSON decoding never does.

what_it_does: Checks that every row has the same column names, then writes the rows as delimited text to a file or stdout, or writes a raw SQL string.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: COLUMN_NAMES is fixed before the check, so set(COLUMN_NAMES) can be built once and reused for every row, which removes one set build of the column names per row. The CSV writer that follows does the same per-row work either way, and the colnames value from transform_to_expression_matrix is a list, so no iterator is consumed twice.

what_it_does: Loads inputs from a JSON file, a JSON string and -i name=value pairs into the input dict, translating dotted stage names on workflows, then checks or prompts for required inputs.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: For a globalworkflow, each dotted -i name builds a fresh DXWorkflow through DXGlobalWorkflow._get_input_name, and that object runs one describe on its first stages access, so k dotted names cost k describes. Holding one underlying handle for the loop, created lazily so the order of errors is unchanged, leaves one describe for all names and the same final value of _workflow_desc_by_region, and it needs no change to get_underlying_workflow.

what_it_does: Stores the executable handle and region, fetches the executable description, and builds the input spec with required, optional and array input lists from it.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The description that get_exec_handler discards (resolver.py line 1259) would have to be handed to ExecutableInputs, which means changing get_exec_handler and its callers in cli/workflow.py, and those are other units. A global workflow description from the resolver also lacks the stages and inputs that get_executable_description appends, so reusing it would not give the same handle state on that path.

what_it_does: Captures the workflow edit version, validates the requested stage changes, resolves any new executable or existing executable inputs, and calls the workflow update API with the captured version.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The editVersion read at line 213 goes through DXObject.__getattr__ and describes the workflow before the no-updates guard at line 220, so a run that only prints No updates requested still makes that request. Moving the read below the guard keeps it ahead of every other call in the update path, so the captured version and the request count on updating runs are unchanged; the one difference is that a failing describe on a no-op run no longer raises.

what_it_does: Resolves each path argument to files and folders, lists matching subfolders per project, checks explicit project membership, and downloads the matches to the destination.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: dxpy.list_subfolders issues a project describe with folders requested on every call, so each path argument fetches the full folder list of its project again. Caching that list once per project and applying the same non-recursive filter that list_subfolders uses returns the same matching folders in the same order, and the first failure still raises at the same path.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The any() at line 254 stops at the first file found in the project, so the common case is one describe rather than one per file. For an explicit project:file-ID path, _check_resolution_needed in resolver.py at lines 703 and 710 does not compare the returned project with the hinted one, so this describe is the only membership test and cannot be dropped.

what_it_does: Checks the destination and the object class, logs debug messages, and calls the database file download for one database object.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The eager format runs once per database file on a short name and costs well under a microsecond, which is not measurable next to the download itself. The lazy form would print the same text, but it saves nothing that matters.

what_it_does: Sets up tab completion, prompts for each missing required input and optionally for optional inputs, then tears completion down.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: init_completer calls readline.write_history_file on the dx history file before clearing history, so skipping it when nothing is prompted would stop a file write that happens today, and the repair must preserve that file effect. The write is one small file per interactive call, so the saving is small as well.

what_it_does: Streams the orgs matching the query and prints them as JSON, as IDs only, or as ID and name lines joined by a delimiter.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: DELIMITER returns a module-level value through one conditional, so the call costs tens of nanoseconds per org row, next to a network page fetch that already produced each row. Hoisting it saves nothing measurable.

what_it_does: Lists the subfolders of a parent folder in a project and reports whether a named child folder exists.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: A folder memo kept inside this function or at module level would serve stale listings to later calls in the long-lived dx shell, so results would change from one command to the next. The batch caller reaches this function through _format_resolution_output and _resolve_folder rather than directly from resolve_multiple_existing_paths, and a per-batch memo would need those two functions changed, each with its own entry.

what_it_does: Resolves a list of input paths into project, folder and object results, describing hash IDs one at a time and batching name lookups into one resolve call.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: A batch describe through system_describe_data_objects would need the per-object project hint and the fallback without it that _check_resolution_needed applies at lines 703 and 710, and the only bulk describe in the repo, in bindings dxdataobject_functions describe, sends neither. A batch call also fails as a whole where each path fails alone today and is swallowed at line 990, so the error path cannot be shown identical from the code.

what_it_does: Looks up a finished job output field, optionally indexed, and describes each data object it names with one request per object.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: A batch describe would have to carry the project hint set at line 572 and keep each element own ResolutionError text, and no batch describe in the repo does either, so output and printed errors cannot be shown identical from the code. The cost is one describe per array element, which is real but bounded by the array length.

what_it_does: Maps a project name or ID string to a project ID, caching unique name matches and querying find_projects for every other name.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Caching ambiguous matches would add a module-level cache that persists across commands in the dx shell, so a project renamed, deleted or created after the first lookup would still resolve from the stale list, where the code today queries again. The repeat query is the behaviour that stays correct in that process model.

what_it_does: Splits a path into project, folder and entity name, handling dxfuse xattr lookups, JSON-encoded links, hash IDs and colon placement.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The two subscripts read distinct keys, project and id, so two getxattr reads happen whether or not the handle is bound once. The repair saves only one handle construction, so the step-1 claim that it halves the reads is wrong.

what_it_does: Splits a string on a character that is not preceded by an odd number of backslashes, and returns the pieces in order.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The copies are of path or name=value strings, so the cost is proportional to length times separator count, which is microseconds for a path. Even a 10 KB -i value with 100 equals signs costs well under a millisecond of byte copying, so the repair is output-identical but saves nothing measurable next to the requests around path resolution.

what_it_does: Returns the index of the last unescaped occurrence of a character in a string, or -1 if there is none.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: string.rfind with an end index returns the same index without the prefix copy, but the copy is of a path-sized string, a few hundred bytes per call, which is far below any measurable cost in path resolution.

what_it_does: Returns the index of the first unescaped occurrence of a character in a string, or -1 if there is none.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The same rfind with an end index gives identical results, but the prefix copy is of a path-sized string, a few hundred bytes per call, which is far below any measurable cost in path resolution.

what_it_does: Returns the project and ID string from a JSON-encoded DNAnexus link, or returns the input unchanged.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: json.loads fails on the first character of an ordinary path and costs microseconds, and a leading-brace guard after whitespace removal would return the same values. The saving per path is far below the describe or list request that follows each path resolution.

what_it_does: Returns the resolution results unchanged when they are unambiguous or the caller wants all of them, and otherwise prompts for a choice or raises.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The any() runs only in the interactive branch, on a list with one entry per candidate, which is a handful of entries at most. The list comprehension costs nothing measurable there.

what_it_does: Walks a resolved input tree and records, for each job-based object reference, the output value it resolves to by describing the referenced job.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each distinct JBOR string triggers its own job_describe, so two inputs that point at different output fields of one job fetch the full job description twice. A per-call cache keyed by job ID, held by a private recursive helper so that the public signature and the single caller in describe.py stay unchanged, makes one describe per job, and failed describes are not cached so error behaviour matches.

what_it_does: Renders each bundledDepends entry of a describe output as a name and ID string, and for file-based bundles reads the AssetBundle property and describes the record to get the asset name.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The property read and the record describe each produce a value the output needs, the record ID and the asset name, and no earlier request in the function repeats either one because every bundle is a different file. There is no duplicate work to remove.

what_it_does: Builds tab-completion matches for a dx path by searching projects, folders and data objects, and returns the matching completed strings.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: find_data_objects takes a single class string (src/python/dxpy/bindings/search.py line 205 sets the query class to one value) and caps each call at 100 results (line 150 here), so merging the classes into one call without a class filter would change which 100 results come back and would fetch objects of other classes. The per-class calls are needed under the current API.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Passing the typed text plus a star as a glob name filter to find_projects returns a superset of the startswith matches, and the kept Python startswith and include_current_proj filters trim it, so the returned matches are the same. Each bare-name Tab press then stops paging through every accessible project with its describe payload. The order of matches follows the server, which needs a platform check.

what_it_does: Builds per-input file descriptors (handler, basename, prefix, path) and the non-file input hash for the bash variable export and the download and mount helpers, by calling get_job_input_filenames and reading the input spec patterns.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The per-file describe is the handler.name read at line 236 inside get_job_input_filenames, which download_all_inputs.py and mount_all_inputs.py also call, so removing it means changing a helper outside this unit. Rebuilding the file list here with one batched describe would drop each link's project (src/python/dxpy/bindings/dxdataobject_functions.py lines 209 to 215), so a cross-project input could be described against the wrong project. The re-read of job_input.json is one local file read and costs little.

what_it_does: Launches one execution per batch row, naming each after the executable name and its batch ID, and returns the list of executions.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: batch_launch_args has already called executable.describe() on the same object through _get_types_for_inputs, and describe() stores its result in _desc for DXApplet, DXApp, DXWorkflow and DXGlobalWorkflow, so reading the cached name removes one describe request per dx run with --batch-tsv. A fallback describe keeps the behaviour when no name is cached, and the only caller, run_batch_all_steps in src/python/dxpy/scripts/dx.py, is unchanged.

what_it_does: Waits for each depends_on entry, which is a local job, a remote job or a data object, to finish or close, printing a line per wait and re-raising any failure with the ID attached.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The describe result stored in desc on line 210 is never read, and handler._wait_on_close() starts with its own state describe (src/python/dxpy/bindings/__init__.py lines 626 to 641 and line 646), so deleting line 210 removes one full describe request per non-job data object and leaves the wait, the printed lines and the error wrapping unchanged. This runs only in local execution.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: A repeated ID in depends_on was already waited on, and a closed data object or a done job stays that way, so the repeat needs no request if the print stays before a skip that keeps the output identical. Repeats come from get_implicit_depends_on appending every occurrence of a link, so the saving is one state request per repeated occurrence.

what_it_does: Returns the object ID of a DNAnexus link value when the linked object is not closed, using one describe call on that object, and returns None otherwise.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: A memo for repeated IDs needs state across the loop in get_implicit_depends_on (lines 165 to 193), which is outside this unit and would need an entry of its own. A module-level cache would go stale across jobs in one local run, so an object that closed later could still be treated as open, adding a dependency and a printed wait line that the current code would not print.

what_it_does: Runs one local job entry point after resolving its inputs and waiting for its dependencies, writes its input and environment files, runs the process, and records its output in job_outputs.json.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each pass is local CPU over small finished-job output dicts with no request, because a remote job reference is replaced in place on its first resolution (resolve_job_references writes back at lines 132 and 141), so later passes repeat no network call. The growth is quadratic in local job count, but local test runs have few jobs, so the saving is negligible.

what_it_does: Handles each streamed log message by storing it and then repainting the whole curses screen, including for METRICS messages that change only the top line.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each refresh rebuilds the visible rows in a curses buffer, and curses sends only the cells that changed, so a METRICS message adds one buffer rebuild and no extra terminal output. A METRICS-only redraw would need its own partial draw path that must match the full draw exactly, for a per-message cost that is small.

what_it_does: Wraps the help text to the screen width with textwrap and draws it on the help screen on each refresh.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The help text is a short constant string wrapped on each refresh while the help screen is open, which costs microseconds. Caching the wrapped lines would need a key on the screen width, which changes on resize, for a saving far below anything measurable.

what_it_does: Suggests the closest known word for a mistyped value by checking the word itself, then its one-edit set, then its two-edit set, and returns the most frequent candidate.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The one-edit set is built here and again inside _known_edits2, but that second build is one call among about 54 times the word length plus 25 calls in the two-edit loop, so the duplicate is well under one percent of the miss path. The path runs only after argparse rejects an invalid choice (src/python/dxpy/scripts/dx.py line 4559), so it runs once per typo.

what_it_does: Returns the known words exactly two edits away from a word by building the one-edit set of the word and of each one-edit candidate.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The repeated first-level set is one call among about 54 times the word length plus 25 calls in the same nested comprehension, so removing it saves well under one percent. The function runs only after an invalid argparse choice, so the saving is negligible.

what_it_does: Lays out an array of rows as a box-drawn text table with column widths set by the widest cell and long cells truncated.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The list copy costs one pointer per row, once per table, and the row loop that follows formats every cell, so the saving is negligible. Replacing it with table[0] would break the callers that pass dict .values() views (src/python/dxpy/scripts/dx_app_wizard.py lines 369 to 375 and src/python/dxpy/cli/parsers.py lines 355 to 365), since those views are not subscriptable.

what_it_does: Removes the session and saved configuration files and, when reset is true, sets every configuration variable to its default, saves them, and leaves the in-memory dxpy state synced.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each of the seven core-variable assignments runs _sync_dxpy_state, which makes a few in-memory assignments and one JSON load, so the six extra syncs cost microseconds in a one-off command. A single sync after the loop would leave the same final state, but the energy it saves is below measurement.

what_it_does: Builds the shell variable definitions for a job input file, skipping any name that collides with an environment variable or an earlier definition.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The value is built before the collision check, so a colliding key has its string built and then dropped. Only keys that match an environment variable or an earlier key take that path, the work is local string quoting with no request (dxlink does not describe), and the saving is microseconds per colliding key.

what_it_does: Rewrites a JSON text so every array with a given name is printed on a single line.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop makes one full-text regex pass per element line of the named array, and its only caller, src/python/dxpy/utils/executable_unbuilder.py line 55, feeds it a small dxapp-style document, so the work is a few regex passes over a few kilobytes. A single-pass rewrite would have to reproduce the greedy match exactly, which is not worth the risk for that saving.

what_it_does: Archives two files in a test project, waits a fixed 10 seconds, checks their archivalState, and checks two error paths of dx archive.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: A fixed sleep costs only idle power, and polling archivalState would replace it with repeated describe requests, which cost real energy, so the sleep is not energy waste under the energy criterion.

what_it_does: Archives matching files through the -a flag and through an interactive confirmation, each followed by a fixed 10 second wait and archivalState checks.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Two fixed sleeps cost only idle power, and polling would replace them with repeated describe requests that cost real energy, so the sleeps are not energy waste under the energy criterion.

what_it_does: Archives a subfolder, then the root with --no-recurse, then the root recursively, with fixed sleeps of 10, 10 and 20 seconds before archivalState checks.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Fixed sleeps cost only idle power, and polling would replace them with repeated describe requests that cost real energy, so the sleeps are not energy waste under the energy criterion.

what_it_does: Archives one file and all copies of another across two projects, with fixed sleeps of 10 and 30 seconds before archivalState checks.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Fixed sleeps cost only idle power, and polling would replace them with repeated describe requests that cost real energy, so the sleeps are not energy waste under the energy criterion.

what_it_does: Archives a project, drives a dry-run unarchive through pexpect, then tags files for unarchival, with fixed sleeps of 15, 20 and 20 seconds before state checks.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Fixed sleeps cost only idle power, and polling would replace them with repeated describe requests that cost real energy, so the sleeps are not energy waste under the energy criterion.

what_it_does: Runs 16 interactive `dx archive` prompts whose path list grows each round, answers n to each, and checks that equivalent spellings of one file or one folder resolve to a single target.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The growing argument list is the point of the test, because each prompt checks that every accumulated spelling still resolves to one target. Resetting the list each round would test each spelling alone and drop that check, and the 16 CLI starts happen once per run of this single test.

what_it_does: Creates a second project before each of the 21 tests in TestDXClientRun and destroys it afterwards, although only two tests read it.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Deferring creation to first access and skipping destruction for the other 19 tests would save 19 CLI starts and 38 API calls per run, and no other module reads the attribute. But run() echoes the command `dx new project other --brief` and its output to stdout, so 19 printed echo blocks per test disappear, which fails criterion (c) on printed output.

what_it_does: Chains two applet jobs and a third dependent job, then polls the second job state every 0.1 s while it is idle, and checks the resolved JBOR text in the describe output.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop calls DXJob.describe about ten times a second with no backoff, while the library's own DXJob.wait_on_done polls every 2 s. Doubling the sleep from 0.1 s to a 2 s cap keeps the same exit test, the same describe result and the same printed output, and it cuts the describe requests issued while the dependent job waits.

what_it_does: Starts a squid proxy, runs a job through `dx ssh` with the proxy, checks proxy failures, then polls `dx find jobs` until the terminated job shows as terminated.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The squid readiness probe is a bounded loop of localhost requests and costs almost nothing. The termination poll does start one dx CLI process per second, which is a real cost, but run() echoes each poll command and its output to stdout, and a repair that drops those CLI calls removes that printed output, which fails criterion (c).

what_it_does: Launches a job that exits with an error under debug-on AppInternalError, polls dxpy.describe once per second until the job reaches debug_hold, and then opens dx ssh to the job.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop calls dxpy.describe every second for as long as the job boots and runs, which can take minutes, and it has no backoff. Growing the sleep from 1 s to a 30 s cap while summing the sleeps against the same 1200 s budget keeps the exit test, the exception type and the printed output, and describe requests drop from one per second to at most one per 30 s during a long boot.

what_it_does: Opens dx ssh sessions with different allow-ssh options, sleeps 5 s before each one closes, and then checks that the job allowSSH list matches the expected IPs.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each fixed sleep gives a spawned dx ssh process time to update allowSSH while the test client sits idle. A polling replacement would add describe requests, which cost network energy, so the only saving is idle power over a few seconds.

what_it_does: Uploads a 5 MiB part and a 1-byte part, runs dx download on a local file truncated in five ways, and after each download checks its MD5 against a digest rebuilt from the two parts.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each rebuild costs one 5 MiB concatenation and one MD5, which one timing run in this environment put at about 19 ms each. Four avoidable rebuilds save well under 0.1 s of CPU, while each dx download in the same test makes network requests and moves the same bytes.

what_it_does: Runs `dx describe` on an analysis in three forms and checks for expected keys in the text and JSON outputs.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: json.loads on describe output of this size takes microseconds, and the repeated parses sit beside three dx describe subprocesses that cost far more energy.

what_it_does: Runs `dx describe` on a job in three forms and checks for verbose-only fields in the text and JSON outputs.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: json.loads on describe output of this size takes microseconds, and the two repeated parses sit beside three dx describe subprocesses that cost far more energy.

what_it_does: Creates a workflow, runs it twice, waits a fixed 20 s before describing each stage job, and checks tags, properties, stage inputs and workflow editing along the way.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Both 20 s sleeps are idle waits for the platform to create a job. Polling would trade that idle time for describe requests, and the net energy saving is small.

what_it_does: Runs four clones of an analysis with different inputs and instance types, waits fixed times, then checks the resulting analysis and job descriptions and a cross-project clone.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The 30 s and 20 s sleeps are idle waits for new jobs to appear on the platform. Polling would add describe requests, so the only saving is idle power.

what_it_does: Runs one workflow with several stage output folder options, waits a fixed 20 s for the stage jobs to be generated, and then checks each analysis stage folder.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The fixed 20 s is an idle wait for the platform to generate jobs. Polling would replace idle time with describe requests, so the net energy saving is small.

what_it_does: Adds, lists and removes workflow stages and checks the workflow description after each change, with dx describe run on the workflow at two points.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each dx describe discards its output, but run() raises CalledProcessError on a nonzero exit. Removing either call removes a check that the workflow describes cleanly, which fails criterion (c) on exception behaviour, and the saving is two CLI starts.

what_it_does: Adds a stage to a new workflow, updates its name, folder, input, instance type and executable through dx update stage, and checks the workflow description after each step.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The variable desc_string is never read, yet the call still checks that dx describe succeeds on a workflow whose stage executable was just deleted. run() raises on a nonzero exit, so removing the assignment removes that exception path.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The discarded dx describe at the top of the test doubles as a check that a new workflow describes cleanly, and run() raises on a nonzero exit. Removing it removes that exception path, and the saving is one CLI start.

what_it_does: Checks that dx update workflow fails on a nonexistent name and on a pipeline record ID, with a dx describe of the record run between the two checks.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The describe output is discarded, but run() raises on a nonzero exit, so the call checks that the record can be described before the update is tried. Removing it removes that check and saves one CLI start.

what_it_does: Builds and runs a global workflow, waits a fixed 5 s for the first stage job to exist, and then checks its describe output and the help text of the workflow.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The 5 s sleep is an idle wait for the platform to create the job. Polling would add describe requests, so the only saving is idle power over a few seconds.

what_it_does: Creates an applet, a workflow, an analysis and two jobs, waits in a retry loop for the analysis stage job to exist, and then checks the counts printed by dx find executions, jobs and analyses.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each miss costs one job_describe request and then a 5 s idle sleep, and the loop makes few requests when the job appears quickly. Shortening the sleep trades idle power for more requests, and the energy at stake is a few seconds of idle power.

what_it_does: Creates a temporary project, a workflow and a runner applet, waits in two retry loops for the analysis and then the stage job to appear, and then checks dx find output for executions, jobs and analyses.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Both loops already poll one request every 5 s, about 0.2 Hz, and the runner must boot a worker first, so the loops sit idle for most of their span. The request rate is already low, so polling less often saves almost nothing.

what_it_does: Starts a squid proxy, waits 1 s, probes localhost every 0.5 s until squid answers, and then builds two proxy environment dictionaries.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The 1 s sleep is idle, and removing it only adds an earlier localhost probe that is refused, which costs microseconds. The readiness loop is already bounded and cheap.

what_it_does: Creates two temporary projects for a test, sets the workspace to the first, and stores the second project ID on the test instance for the matching teardown to destroy.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Only a handful of the 91 tests in the twelve classes that call this helper read second_proj_id (TestDXProject, TestDXRecord, TestDXSearch and TestDataobjectFunctions), yet every test creates and destroys it. Deferring creation needs either a descriptor installed on each test class or edits to the eight other setUp callers, and both lie outside this unit, so this needs its own unit.

what_it_does: Creates one record, sleeps 2 s, then checks find_data_objects time-offset filters against the record age, so the sleep sets the age the asserts require.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The sleep is idle wait, which draws little energy, and the asserts need the record to be more than 100 ms old, so the sleep only sets a floor on that age. Shortening it changes wall-clock time, not energy.

what_it_does: Runs two fresh python3 subprocesses that import dxpy and print DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE, once with DX_JOB_ID set and once without, because that constant is fixed at import time.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: dxfile.py reads dxpy.JOB_ID at import, so each case needs a fresh interpreter. An in-process importlib.reload would re-run the package import and change dxpy module state that other tests in the same process share.

what_it_does: Creates 1005 records with one API call each, resolves 1005 names in batches of 1000, and checks the results at indices 200 and 1003.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Create records only at indices 200 and 1003 and pass all 1005 names, since the earlier asserts show a missing name resolves to an empty list. The 1000-entry batch boundary is still crossed, so index 1003 stays in the second batch, and about 1003 create requests per run are removed. Needs the DNAnexus platform.

what_it_does: Resolves a dataset or cohort record, builds a vizserver payload from the filters, sends a raw SQL query and a data query, and compares the SQL and, when data_test is set, the data with expected output.
